hints: Start with state at room temperature. Only one of the four possible compounds is a liquid, so match that first to narrow the choices.
Think about which compounds simply dissolve in water without reacting, and what pH you would expect from a Group 2 hydroxide solution versus a Group 1 chloride solution.
Recall what happens when covalent chlorides and acidic oxides react vigorously with water, and what acidic gases or acids are produced.
Use solubility to separate the two solids that dissolve. One dissolves completely to give a neutral solution, the other is only sparingly soluble so some white solid remains in alkaline solution.
walkthrough:
Use state to spot T immediately**
Look at the table. R, S and U are all solids, but T is a liquid. From your list, $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ are all solids at room temperature. Only $\text{SiCl}_4$ is a liquid. That alone tells you T is $\text{SiCl}_4$. This also fits the observation of misty fumes and a vigorous reaction, because $\text{SiCl}_4$ hydrolyses: $$\text{SiCl}_4(l) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2(s) + 4\text{HCl}(g)$$ The $\text{HCl}$ appears as misty white fumes.

Pick out the neutral dissolving solid as S**
S is a solid that simply disappears to give a neutral solution. That is classic physical dissolving with no hydrolysis. $\text{NaCl}$ is very soluble and gives $\text{Na}^+(aq)$ and $\text{Cl}^-(aq)$, neither of which reacts with water, so pH stays at 7. So S is $\text{NaCl}$.

Pick out the sparingly soluble alkali as R**
R is a solid that gives an alkaline colourless solution but some white solid remains. $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ releases $\text{OH}^-(aq)$ ions, so the solution is alkaline: $$\text{Ba(OH)}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Ba}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{OH}^-(aq)$$ Barium hydroxide is only sparingly soluble in cold water, so excess stays as white solid. That matches R exactly, so R is $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$.

Assign the vigorous acidic oxide as U**
That leaves U. U is a solid that reacts vigorously to give an acidic colourless solution. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is an acidic oxide that reacts exothermically with water to form phosphoric acid: $$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}(s) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4(aq)$$ This gives a strongly acidic solution with no solid left, exactly as described. So U is $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$.

Final answer: R: $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ OR barium hydroxide
S: $\text{NaCl}$ OR sodium chloride
T: $\text{SiCl}_4$ OR silicon(IV) chloride
U: $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ OR phosphorus(V) oxide

hints: Recall the hydrolysis equation for sample T identified in (a)(i) and think about which product is a white solid rather than a gas or solution.
walkthrough:
Write out what T makes with water**
You found T is $\text{SiCl}_4$. When it meets water it does not just dissolve, it is hydrolysed completely. The silicon ends up bonded to oxygen as a solid, while the chlorine ends up as $\text{HCl}$ fumes: $$\text{SiCl}_4(l) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2(s) + 4\text{HCl}(g)$$ The white solid you see is therefore $\text{SiO}_2$.

hints: Think about the acid formed when the acidic oxide identified as sample U reacts fully with excess cold water.
walkthrough:
Link the acidic solution to its parent acid**
You found U is $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$. Acidic oxides reform their parent acid with water. Here: $$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}(s) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4(aq)$$ So the colourless acidic solution is phosphoric acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$.
Final answer: phosphoric acid / phosphoric(V) acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$)

hints: Picture a ceramic mug or tile and recall how it behaves on heating and whether it lets electricity pass.
walkthrough:
Remember what makes a ceramic a ceramic**
$\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ are giant ionic lattices. The strong ionic bonds in three dimensions need huge energy to break, so they stay solid to very high temperatures and stay hard and strong. Because ions are locked in place in the solid, there are no mobile charges, so they cannot conduct electricity. Any one of high melting point, electrical insulator, hard, strong or brittle is correct.
Final answer: High melting point OR electrical insulator / non-conductor of electricity OR hard / strong / brittle / retains strength at high temperature

hints: Look for another Period 3 oxide with a giant lattice that has a very high melting point like $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$.
walkthrough:
Find the other giant Period 3 oxide**
Run through Period 3 oxides: $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_2$. $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ are already given. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is ionic but lower melting, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{SO}_2$ are simple molecular. Only $\text{SiO}_2$ is left with a giant covalent network of strong $\text{Si-O}$ bonds, very high melting point and ceramic behaviour. So the answer is $\text{SiO}_2$.

hints: Assume 100 g of oxide so the percentages become masses, then find the mass of oxygen by subtraction from 100.
Convert each mass to moles by dividing by the relative atomic mass, using $A_r$ of W = 183.8 and $A_r$ of O = 16.0.
Divide both mole values by the smaller one to get the simplest whole number ratio of W to O and write it as $\text{W}_x\text{O}_y$.
walkthrough:
Turn percentages into masses**
Imagine you have 100 g of $\text{W}_x\text{O}_y$. Then you have 79.29 g of W. Everything else is oxygen, so: $$\text{mass of O} = 100 - 79.29 = 20.71\text{ g}$$ This step is easy to forget, but you cannot get moles of oxygen without its mass.

Convert to moles**
Now divide by $A_r$ values to get moles. Use W = 183.8 and O = 16.0: $$\text{mol W} = \frac{79.29}{183.8} = 0.4314\text{ mol}$$ $$\text{mol O} = \frac{20.71}{16.0} = 1.294\text{ mol}$$ Keep extra figures for now to avoid rounding error.

Simplify to the whole number ratio**
Divide both by the smallest, 0.4314: $$\frac{0.4314}{0.4314} = 1$$ $$\frac{1.294}{0.4314} = 3.00$$ So W : O = 1 : 3. That gives the empirical formula $\text{WO}_3$.

Final answer: mass of O = 100 - 79.29 = 20.71 g
mol W = 79.29 / 183.8 = 0.4314 mol
mol O = 20.71 / 16.0 = 1.294 mol
ratio W : O = 0.4314 : 1.294 = 1 : 3
empirical formula = $\text{WO}_3$
